raw.champion: Congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries
raw.rationale: The patient's echocardiogram shows the right atrium and right ventricle on the left side, and the left atrium and left ventricle on the right side with its apex directed to the right, which is consistent with congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries. The ECG findings also support this diagnosis, with a wide complex rhythm and right bundle branch block morphology.

rejected.label: Dextrocardia with situs solitus
rejected.why: Dextrocardia would typically show the heart in the right chest with normal atrial and ventricular positions, which is not the case here

rejected.label: Situs ambiguus
rejected.why: Situs ambiguus would typically show ambiguous or indeterminate positioning of the atria and ventricles, which is not consistent with the clear reversal seen in this patient

rejected.label: Ivemark syndrome
rejected.why: Ivemark syndrome is a rare condition that typically presents with polysplenia and complex congenital heart disease, which is not suggested by the patient's echocardiogram or ECG findings

rejected.label: Ebstein's anomaly
rejected.why: Ebstein's anomaly would typically show abnormal tricuspid valve formation and a small right ventricle, which is not consistent with the patient's echocardiogram findings
